notes: BSB flagged mallon as represented and it is a genuine error, not a convention difference. The ASV's comparative 'better' spells kalon and mallon together, and the chapter's own parallel verses prove it: with mallon present the ASV writes 'better' (9.42), and where the Greek has no mallon it writes 'good ... rather than' with the supplied 'rather' folded onto e (9.43, 9.45, 9.47). Under rule 39's test some part of the single English word answers to each source token, so the pair is one `aligned` unit headed on 'better', source head on the lexical kalon (rule 10). Rule 15 permits the discontinuity. All other units of the verse are unchanged.
